points.text: The discussion is a sustainability pitch.
The main aim is to understand what sustainability is.
Sustainability has three pillars: Environment, Social, and Governance (E-S-E).
The three pillars of sustainability are Environment, Social, and Governance.
Governance includes laws, compliance, standards, and frameworks.
The social part is related to humans, employees, vendors, stakeholders, and management.
The environment part is about affecting society and the planet.
The speaker suggests giving sustainability consulting to Kiran Hospital.
The speaker thinks that sustainable capital is important for sub-world countries.
Sustainability was a burden for the sustainable economy in 1997.
The U.N. had to judge the climate changes in 1997.
The Paris agreement was released in 2016.
The Paris agreement aimed to not increase the average temperature by more than 2.5 degrees.
Targets were set for every country in 2016.
Countries took steps to achieve the targets.
The progress is monitored every year.
India targeted to reduce its energy consumption by 50% by 2030.
The speaker thinks that companies should support the government in achieving sustainability targets.
The speaker is worried that every industry will be affected by sustainability regulations.
The speaker thinks that companies should be prepared to adapt to the changing regulations.
ESG is used to measure a company's sustainability performance.
Investors are now looking at ESG performance in addition to financial performance.
The top 1000 companies are required to report their ESG performance.
The speaker thinks that they can help companies achieve their sustainability targets.
The speaker suggests creating a board for audience and education on sustainability.
The speaker thinks that they should have some products in line for ESG.
The speaker suggests developing an initial version of an ESG product within 6 months.
The speaker thinks that they should audit the framework for ESG.
The speaker suggests automating the process of collecting data for ESG.
The speaker mentions that they are working with operational technology (OT) and not just IT.
